claim: CLI-BEHIND <n> embeds a literal commit-count magnitude in its finding string, but STALE/MISSING/EXTRA (the dominant, content-hash finding class) carry only a bare path with no magnitude — so a file that stays stale while diverging further every day produces an identical --signature forever, and mk-rd1x's STANDING mechanism permanently swallows it after the first warn, even though the plan's own line 74 claims growth re-fires the check.

evidence: Line 74 states '...so an unchanged drift becomes warn + STANDING under mk-rd1x and a grown one fails again' — true only for CLI-BEHIND <n>, which carries a variable count, and false for STALE/MISSING/EXTRA, whose format (line 68) has no magnitude term at all. Same root cause as round-0 f-017 (parse_signature has no magnitude term) — this finding sharpens it with the concrete CLI-BEHIND vs STALE/MISSING/EXTRA contrast.
